title: Timekeeping and Billing Narratives
answer: Timekeeping and Billing Narratives covers how law firms and legal departments record billable work and describe it on invoices. It includes time capture, narrative drafting, task and activity coding, invoice review, and the link between entries and client billing guidelines. It also covers alternative fee arrangements, budgets, and write-offs where narratives support or challenge charges. The topic sits in legal operations and touches finance, practice management, and client service.

sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: These systems run on time and billing platforms, practice management suites, e-billing portals, and document or email stores that supply context. Cloud hosting, single sign-on, role-based access, encryption, and audit logging are common controls. Integrations use APIs and file formats such as LEDES for invoice exchange. Mobile and desktop clients, calendar and matter systems, and voice capture tools feed the pipeline.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Work begins with capturing time from calendars, documents, calls, and manual timers. AI models can draft narratives from matter context, suggest task codes, and flag entries that miss client guidelines. Rules engines and templates enforce billing formats, while human reviewers approve, edit, or reject suggestions. The output is a reviewed invoice or time entry with a traceable link to source activity.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk center on privilege, confidentiality, and client consent for using AI on matter data. Provenance matters because a narrative must reflect actual work, not a generated approximation, and audit trails should show who edited what. Outside counsel guidelines, fee disputes, and professional conduct rules shape what can be billed and how AI use is disclosed. Data retention, access controls, and vendor terms determine whether client information stays protected.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Expect tighter integration between time capture and matter systems, with narratives generated closer to the work. E-billing platforms will likely add more automated guideline checks and anomaly detection. Clients and firms will push for clearer standards on AI-assisted entries and disclosure. The site tracks 215 compliance and regulation pages, which reflects how quickly billing and AI rules are accumulating.
